title: India Inc Revenue Growth Hits Two-Year High but Profit Squeeze Deepens on Rising Costs
excerpt: Corporate India's top line surged 11-11.5% in Q1 FY27 driven by pricing power, but margins contracted sharply as the West Asia conflict pushed input costs higher.
body:
• India Inc's revenue grew 11-11.5% year-on-year in Q1 FY27 (April-June 2026), the fastest pace in eight quarters and a two-year high, according to Crisil Intelligence.
  • Pricing replaced volume as the primary growth driver, with sectors like aluminium, steel, cement, and airlines passing higher costs to consumers.
  • Despite strong top-line growth, EBITDA margins contracted 75-100 basis points as companies absorbed rising fuel, freight, and feedstock costs from the West Asia conflict.
  • Financial companies were the outlier — BFSI firms posted 25% profit growth while non-financial companies saw net profit fall nearly 20%.

Revenue Growth Hits Two-Year High

Corporate India's revenue growth accelerated to its fastest pace in two years during the June quarter, even as the West Asia conflict pushed input costs sharply higher. India Inc's aggregate revenue rose 11-11.5% year-on-year in Q1 FY27, up from 9.6% in the preceding March quarter, according to an analysis by Crisil Intelligence covering more than 400 companies across 47 sectors.

A separate Mint analysis of 393 companies that have reported standalone results showed aggregate total income rising 18% year-on-year — the fastest pace in at least three years. But the top-line strength masked a deeper problem: expenditure climbed an even steeper 26.5%, leaving profits largely flat.

Pricing Power Takes the Wheel

For the first time in two years, pricing rather than volume drove revenue growth. Companies in aluminium, steel, cement, airlines, fertilisers, and gems and jewellery raised prices to offset higher raw material costs, according to Sehul Bhatt, Director at Crisil Intelligence.

"For much of the past two years, revenue growth was powered largely by volume. But this time around, pricing was the primary driver, contributing more to revenue growth than volume."

— Sehul Bhatt, Director, Crisil Intelligence

The automobile sector led the charge, posting 22-24% revenue growth supported by GST-led demand, strong passenger vehicle and two-wheeler sales, and selective price increases. Primary aluminium revenue surged 51-53% year-on-year on supply disruptions and firmer global prices. Telecom services grew 10-11%, driven by premiumisation and subscriber upgrades.

The Margin Problem

The revenue surge did not translate into earnings growth. Crisil estimates aggregate EBITDA margins contracted 75-100 basis points year-on-year as companies absorbed rising costs of industrial diesel, commercial LPG, freight, packaging, and feedstock.

The pain was starkest when financial companies were excluded. The 310 non-BFSI companies in Mint's analysis posted a 26% jump in total income — the strongest in nearly three years — but expenditure rose 35%, dragging net profit down almost 20%. Airlines faced a roughly 1,000 basis points decline in EBITDA margin due to aviation turbine fuel costs. Tyre makers saw 200-300 basis points of margin compression from rising rubber and carbon black prices.

UltraTech Cement converted nearly 20% revenue growth into just 7% profit growth. Reliance Industries reported nearly 30% revenue growth but net profit fell 26%. Dr. Reddy's and Cipla saw profits plunge 86% and 34%, respectively, as the generic Revlimid windfall faded.

Banks Carry the Earnings Story

Financial companies told a different story entirely. The 83 BFSI firms in Mint's sample reported just 6% income growth, but expenditure rose only 2%, pushing net profit up nearly 25% — the strongest pace in two years.

ICICI Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, and Axis Bank posted 16-26% growth in net profit, anchoring Nifty 50 earnings. Analysts attributed the strength to lower credit costs, healthy loan growth, and disciplined cost control. Non-banking financial companies delivered 20-35% earnings growth, supported by loan growth normalization in unsecured lending.

"Companies with stronger brands and pricing power were better placed to protect margins through calibrated price hikes, better product mix and cost-saving measures."

— Shripal Shah, MD and CEO, Kotak Securities

What's Next

The outlook hinges on three factors, according to Crisil: the extent of further price increases and their impact on demand, companies' ability to protect volumes while recovering costs, and the pace at which fuel and freight costs normalize. The southwest monsoon's trajectory will also be critical for rural demand and food inflation.

The Street expects Nifty 50 earnings to grow about 14% in FY27. But Gautam Duggad of Motilal Oswal warns that a prolonged period of elevated energy prices could trigger another round of earnings downgrades. Margin recovery, particularly for commodity-sensitive sectors, depends on geopolitical developments in West Asia and the trajectory of crude oil prices.
nri_angle: The earnings season matters for NRI investors with Indian equity portfolios; the divergence between strong revenue and weak profits signals selective opportunities in BFSI while commodities face headwinds.
author: Diaspora Desk
